brief: Goldman desks track a Hormuz-conflict oil premium as Brent hit $117/bbl (+$7 this week) after Iran claimed seven tankers struck overnight, a Houthi drone hit Shaybah, and the US began evacuating diplomats from Saudi Arabia. Goldman's oil trader says the market already prices >$20/bbl of risk premium, with all-out war implying $120+ and fundamentals alone implying the low-$90s. Privorotsky frames outcomes as binary: a clean, limited strike could trigger a sell-the-news unwind of the premium, while a hit on energy chokepoints would leave global balances severely constrained. Futures price the war harder than physical flows do (record backwardation, 54.9% implied vol), while Saudi CDS and bonds widen and ENI banks a refining-margin windfall. Timing is split: the IDF reportedly sees no need to strike before the Knesset election, but the US and Israel have plans for after the midterms, implying the premium's carry cost persists. Separately, Goldman says Europe enters winter with 14-year-low gas inventories against a Hormuz LNG risk comparable in scale to 2022's Russian cutoff, but forecasts TTF easing to 70 EUR/MWh (vs 87 now) since higher US LNG supply offsets lower Qatari volumes, with a cold-winter case capped at 150 EUR/MWh, still well below 2022.
